articles.headline: La Xunta autoriza jaulas-trampa para capturar jabalíes en el entorno de Lugo
articles.subtitle: La autorización tiene un año de vigencia y llega tras las quejas por manadas en los barrios del sur y el suroeste, un área que el PSOE local cifra en más de 220 hectáreas. La UICON instalará y vigilará las trampas; el Concello pondrá el cebo.
articles.body:
La Xunta de Galicia ha autorizado al Concello de Lugo la instalación de jaulas-trampa para controlar la población de jabalíes en el entorno urbano y periurbano de la ciudad. La autorización, concedida a través de la Consellería de Medio Ambiente e Cambio Climático, tendrá una vigencia de un año y responde a la petición del gobierno local para mitigar el riesgo que la presencia de estos animales supone para peatones y conductores.

La ubicación de los dispositivos se acordará entre personal municipal y la Unidade de Investigación para a Conservación da Natureza (UICON) de la Xunta. Serán agentes de ese servicio quienes instalen, vigilen y hagan el seguimiento de las trampas, y quienes avisen al Ayuntamiento en el momento en que entren jabalíes.

El Concello se ocupará del cebado, siguiendo las indicaciones técnicas de la UICON, y del traslado de los ejemplares capturados, cuyo destino determinará personal facultativo veterinario. Las jaulas son de grandes dimensiones, capaces de capturar una camada completa de una sola vez.

## Desbroces, arqueros y críticas del PSOE

La autorización se suma al plan que el gobierno local presentó el viernes, que combina el desbroce de parcelas abandonadas, un bando para recordar a los propietarios su obligación de mantenerlas limpias y la captura mediante arqueros, ya en marcha con varios ejemplares abatidos. El Concello coordina las actuaciones con el Hospital Veterinario Rof Codina, la Asociación Galega de Caza y la Asociación de Tecores de Galicia.

La oposición socialista considera insuficiente el dispositivo. Su portavoz adjunta, Ana González Abelleira, calificó la situación de «máxima gravedad» y reclamó brigadas municipales de control y seguimiento, con supervisión nocturna de la Policía Local, para las manadas que ya entran en las zonas sur y suroeste de la ciudad.

articles.headline: La Diputación reactiva la residencia de Guitiriz con 3,25 millones más
articles.subtitle: La junta de gobierno resuelve el contrato con la anterior adjudicataria, que dejó la obra por debajo del 40% tras dos años, y encarga a Tragsa su remate. El centro tendrá 46 plazas y un plazo de ejecución de 18 meses.
articles.body:
La Diputación de Lugo ha desbloqueado la construcción de la residencia de mayores de Guitiriz, paralizada desde que la anterior adjudicataria incumplió los plazos. La junta de gobierno aprobó el viernes la resolución de aquel contrato —la empresa está en concurso de acreedores— y un nuevo convenio de 3,25 millones de euros para completar las obras de la Casa da Botica, que contará con 46 plazas.

El proyecto se adjudicó en 2023 por 1,9 millones y un plazo inicial de 18 meses, después ampliado otros nueve. Al agotarse ese periodo la ejecución no alcanzaba el 40%, lo que llevó a la Diputación a resolver el contrato. La institución provincial asumirá ahora la totalidad del sobrecoste, hasta 3,13 millones, mientras el Ayuntamiento mantiene su aportación de algo más de 115.000 euros. La empresa pública Tragsa ejecutará los trabajos en un máximo de 18 meses.

## Carreteras, museo y piragüismo

La misma sesión sirvió para impulsar cuatro actuaciones en la red viaria provincial por más de 836.000 euros. Los trabajos rehabilitarán más de 16 kilómetros de carreteras en Taboada, Quiroga, Mondoñedo y Ourol, con un plazo de ejecución de cuatro meses. También se adjudicó la reforma integral de los jardines del Museo Provincial por 138.531 euros y la de la Escuela Provincial de Piragüismo, por 314.711 euros.

articles.headline: La jueza de Ceuta reclama datos a 31 organismos sobre Marruecos y cita a Vivas
articles.subtitle: María Tardón, magistrada de la Audiencia Nacional, dirigió el martes un auto sin precedentes a Policía, Guardia Civil, Ejército y CNI. El presidente de Ceuta y el ex jefe de Gabinete del delegado del Gobierno declararán el 30 de septiembre.
articles.body:
La magistrada de la Audiencia Nacional María Tardón ha dirigido un auto sin precedentes a 31 organismos de seguridad del Estado para esclarecer las responsabilidades de Marruecos y del Gobierno en la entrada masiva de inmigrantes en Ceuta. Entre los destinatarios figuran la Policía Nacional, la Guardia Civil, el Ejército, el Centro Nacional de Inteligencia y el Centro Nacional de Inmigración y Fronteras.

El procedimiento 46/2026, instruido por el Juzgado Central de Instrucción número 3, se abrió el 31 de julio y el 7 de septiembre la jueza ratificó la competencia de la Audiencia Nacional. El auto también alcanza al Estado Mayor de la Defensa, al que reclama las imágenes satelitales, y a empresas privadas como HI Iberia.

## Vivas y Sanz, citados el 30 de septiembre

La jueza ha citado como testigos al presidente de Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas, y al ex jefe de Gabinete del delegado del Gobierno en la ciudad autónoma, Gonzalo Sanz, que dimitió ratificando que la víspera del asalto había trasladado al delegado la información remitida por el CNI. Ambas comparecencias, consideradas prioritarias, están fijadas para el 30 de septiembre.

Tardón aprecia indicios de delitos contra la paz o la independencia del Estado, contra los derechos de los ciudadanos extranjeros en conexión con homicidios imprudentes y de organización criminal. El auto advierte de que la inacción ante una información cierta podría generar responsabilidad en la muerte de 83 personas en el lado español de la frontera. Los requerimientos se extienden a Meta, TikTok, Telegram, Google y Apple para conservar los datos de la convocatoria.

articles.headline: Más de 1.000 menores siguen deambulando por Ceuta 50 días después
articles.subtitle: La ciudad autónoma ha filiado a 2.200 menores no acompañados y solo dispone de 29 plazas ordinarias. Juventud da al PP un máximo de dos meses antes de forzar los traslados a la península.
articles.body:
Los alrededor de mil menores que aún viven en la calle en Ceuta pasan los días atrapados en un bucle que se repite cualquier jornada: acuden a la Jefatura Superior de Policía para ser filiados, no logran entrar, se les remite a unos centros de acogida sin plazas disponibles y vuelven a la calle.

El perfil de los recién llegados ha cambiado desde la entrada masiva de finales de julio: ahora son mayoritariamente varones de entre 14 y 17 años. Antes de julio había unos 700 menores no acompañados en el sistema de acogida ceutí; a ellos se sumaron en torno a 1.300 que cruzaron entre el 30 y el 31 de ese mes. Hoy hay 2.200 menores filiados.

## La batalla política del traslado

Ceuta solo dispone de 29 plazas ordinarias y su capacidad está desbordada. El presidente de la ciudad, Juan Jesús Vivas, reclama ahora que todos los menores sean devueltos a Marruecos y se opone a que sean derivados a la península. Su partido gobierna once comunidades, cuatro de ellas en coalición con Vox, que presiona con el rechazo a la inmigración como bandera.

El Ministerio de Juventud e Infancia plantea dos vías: convenios de colaboración entre autonomías o la aplicación del artículo 35 de la ley de extranjería, que obliga a realojarlos. La semana pasada salieron cinco niñas hacia Navarra. El lunes empezaron a tramitarse diez expedientes de repatriación y el mando único espera las primeras resoluciones esta semana.

articles.headline: Un incendio en la clínica psiquiátrica Padre Menni de Pamplona deja un muerto
articles.subtitle: El fuego, declarado sobre las 20:55 en una habitación, obligó a reubicar a medio centenar de pacientes. El balance de heridos oscila entre los siete hospitalizados que reporta EFE y los 18 que después comunicó Europa Press.
articles.body:
Una persona ha fallecido en el incendio que se declaró en torno a las 20:55 horas en una habitación de la clínica psiquiátrica Padre Menni, en el Paseo de los Enamorados de Pamplona. El fuego obligó a reubicar a alrededor de medio centenar de pacientes, que no pudieron pasar la noche en el centro.

Las cifras de heridos difieren entre fuentes. EFE y los medios que citan su información hablan de siete personas trasladadas al hospital por inhalación de humo, mientras que Europa Press elevó el balance a 18 heridas, una de ellas en estado grave e ingresada en la UCI del Hospital Universitario de Navarra.

El incendio, según Europa Press, se originó en una habitación de la planta baja del edificio Granada y la propagación del humo causó daños importantes en las instalaciones. Hasta el lugar se desplazaron dotaciones de los parques de bomberos de Trinitarios y Cordovilla, dos ambulancias de soporte vital avanzado, seis de soporte vital básico y un equipo médico.

La Policía Nacional se ha hecho cargo de la investigación para esclarecer el origen del siniestro; la Policía Municipal de Pamplona colaboró en el operativo. Las primeras hipótesis apuntan a que el fuego pudo ser provocado. La clínica Padre Menni, de las Hermanas Hospitalarias, es un centro de referencia en Navarra en la atención a personas con enfermedad mental.

articles.headline: Podemos lanza primarias abiertas mientras Sumar sigue sin candidato
articles.subtitle: Irene Montero propone que toda la izquierda elija en urnas abiertas al cabeza de lista. Los cuatro partidos de la alianza que dirigía Yolanda Díaz, sin líder desde hace más de 200 días, se fijan ahora octubre.
articles.body:
La izquierda a la izquierda del PSOE afronta el último curso antes de las elecciones generales sin candidato y con las relaciones entre sus dos grandes espacios más tensas que nunca. Podemos ha oficializado a Irene Montero como su referente electoral y ha propuesto unas primarias abiertas a toda la ciudadanía para elegir al cabeza de lista de una candidatura unitaria.

Los partidos que integran Sumar —Movimiento Sumar, IU, Más Madrid y los Comuns— rechazan ese método. Sostienen que su hoja de ruta, en marcha desde hace un año, pasa primero por un acuerdo entre organizaciones y después por consensuar el sistema de listas. Fuentes del espacio admiten que la decisión puede alargarse hasta octubre.

Han pasado más de 200 días desde que Yolanda Díaz anunció que no repetiría como candidata y ningún nombre ha dado el paso. El ministro Pablo Bustinduy, el preferido, lo descartó en marzo; Mónica García volvió a la política madrileña; el líder de IU, Antonio Maíllo, se ha autodescartado esta semana; y Ernest Urtasun mantiene un silencio ambiguo.

Podemos ha colocado además a Ione Belarra como candidata a la Comunidad de Madrid y a Pablo Fernández al Ayuntamiento de la capital para 2027. IU reúne este domingo a su Coordinadora Federal para fijar el calendario de sus propias primarias internas.

articles.headline: El BOE prorroga hasta el 7 de octubre los controles a los viajeros de Italia
articles.subtitle: La Orden INT/977/2026, firmada por Marlaska, extiende desde el 23 de septiembre el restablecimiento temporal de los controles en aeropuertos y puertos con conexión directa. Es la réplica a la suspensión de Schengen que aplica Roma.
articles.body:
El Boletín Oficial del Estado publicó el sábado la Orden INT/977/2026, de 16 de septiembre, por la que se prorroga el restablecimiento temporal de los controles fronterizos en las fronteras interiores aéreas y marítimas españolas respecto a los pasajeros procedentes de Italia. La medida, firmada por el ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, estará en vigor desde las 00:00 del 23 de septiembre hasta las 24:00 del 7 de octubre.

La decisión responde a la réplica italiana. Tras la crisis migratoria de Ceuta, Roma suspendió de facto la libre circulación de Schengen con España y empezó a controlar a los viajeros procedentes del país. España reintrodujo sus propios controles el 8 de agosto y desde entonces ambos gobiernos los prorrogan de forma recíproca.

El texto justifica la prórroga porque subsisten «las razones de urgencia y de amenaza grave para el orden público y la seguridad interior» que motivaron la medida, en aplicación de los artículos 25 y 26 del Código de fronteras Schengen. Añade que la prolongación será objeto de evaluación permanente y quedará sin efecto antes de la fecha prevista si desaparecen las amenazas.

La orden precisa que el final del periodo determinará el levantamiento automático de los controles, sin necesidad de resolución expresa, y que la medida no podrá prorrogarse de forma automática. Italia ha asegurado que sus controles han afectado a más de 180.000 viajeros procedentes de España, con 31 entradas rechazadas y seis detenciones.

articles.headline: Muere una senderista de 71 años al despeñarse en la Ruta del Cares
articles.subtitle: La mujer, de nacionalidad noruega, se colocaba una mochila de gran peso cuando perdió el equilibrio y cayó, a cuatro kilómetros del inicio del recorrido en Pocebos, en el concejo asturiano de Cabrales.
articles.body:
Una senderista de 71 años y nacionalidad noruega falleció este sábado mientras recorría la ruta del Cares, en el concejo asturiano de Cabrales, según informó el Servicio de Emergencias del Principado de Asturias (SEPA). El suceso ocurrió en torno a las 13.02 horas en uno de los tramos más transitados de los Picos de Europa.

La mujer se encontraba a cuatro kilómetros del inicio del recorrido desde Pocebos, pasada la majada de Culiembro, cuando se cayó. Según relataron las personas que llamaron al 112 de Asturias, estaba colocándose una mochila de gran peso y se desestabilizó, lo que provocó la caída.

Efectivos del SEPA acudieron al lugar con el helicóptero de rescate. También se desplazó hasta la zona el Grupo de Rescate e Intervención en Montaña (GREIM) de la Guardia Civil, que se hará cargo del levantamiento del cadáver.

articles.headline: Robinson tells DUP conference unionists must not 'gift wrap' seats to rivals
articles.subtitle: The DUP leader appeals for closer co-operation between unionist parties before next May's assembly and council elections, and says the party was "deceived and let down" by Jeffrey Donaldson.
articles.body:
Gavin Robinson has used his party conference speech to call for closer co-operation between Northern Ireland's unionist parties before next May's assembly and council elections. The DUP leader told delegates that unionism "must not gift wrap seats to Sinn Féin" or Alliance.

"I am committed to working constructively and engaging again with other unionist parties, as we have before, to secure the election of the largest possible number of pro-union candidates," he said. Robinson also urged voters to transfer to other pro-union candidates and said constituencies should not be "flooded" with unionist candidates.

The DUP believes the split unionist vote has handed seats to its opponents in constituencies such as Lagan Valley and North Antrim, both of which the party lost at the last general election. Similar appeals have fallen flat before, and Robinson is speaking from a position of relative weakness.

He also addressed the conviction of his predecessor, Jeffrey Donaldson, for child sex offences including rape. The Belfast Telegraph reported that Robinson told the conference the party had been "deceived and let down" by Donaldson's "vile actions".

On immigration, Robinson said people's fears should not be dismissed: "Controlling immigration is not extreme... Fairness is not intolerance. Common sense deserves a voice; and we will be that voice." The DUP also faces pressure from a resurgent Ulster Unionist Party under its new leader Jon Burrows and from Jim Allister's TUV.

articles.headline: Houthis claim missile and drone strikes on Riyadh and Aramco's Yanbu port
articles.subtitle: Saudi air defences say they intercepted a ballistic missile over the capital, where a fuel depot blaze sent black smoke over King Khalid airport. Air raid alerts sounded in Riyadh for the first time since July.
articles.body:
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis say they launched ballistic and cruise missiles and drones at "sensitive sites" in Riyadh and at Aramco oil facilities in the Red Sea port of Yanbu. Saudi authorities said air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired at the capital, and reported stopping further attacks over Bish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu.

A column of black smoke rose from fuel tanks near King Khalid International Airport on Saturday, where flights were temporarily disrupted and the tracking site FlightRadar24 listed "major problems". Overnight air raid alerts had warned residents of a "hostile aerial threat" — the first such sirens in the capital since the Houthis stepped up their attacks on Saudi Arabia in July.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea said the strikes were a response to what he called Saudi Arabia's criminal attempts to target Sanaa, and accused Riyadh of carrying out 300 strikes across Yemen in a week. The Saudi-led coalition called the attack "terrorist and aggressive behaviour" and accused the rebels of targeting civilians.

The US state department urged Americans in the Middle East to "exercise vigilance", warning the conflict "has the potential to escalate rapidly" and telling citizens to reconsider travel to the region. A truce between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, agreed in 2022, collapsed in July after the rebels allowed an Iranian plane to land in Sanaa.

articles.headline: Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania vote as Merz's future hangs in the balance
articles.subtitle: Two state elections come a fortnight after the AfD's best ever result in Saxony-Anhalt. The anti-immigration party is hoping for further gains that would deepen the pressure on the chancellor.
articles.body:
Voters in Berlin and in the largely rural state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania go to the polls on Sunday in two elections that will test the leadership of Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Both contests come a fortnight after the far-right, anti-immigration Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) scored its highest ever result in Saxony-Anhalt.

The AfD, which is pro-Kremlin and hostile to immigration, is hoping to make sweeping gains again. Public support for the party has surged through the year, and polling suggests both ballots could add to the pressure on Merz's governing coalition in Berlin.

Merz closed his campaign with a rally in the capital, where the Christian Democrats are fighting to hold ground. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania the campaign has been dominated by the state of the economy and by the AfD's calls for a tougher line on migration.

The results will be read as a mid-term verdict on a chancellor who took office promising to revive Europe's largest economy and to curb irregular migration. A strong AfD showing would sharpen the debate over how mainstream parties should handle the far right ahead of further regional ballots later in the year.

The party has also been buoyed by its opposition to German military aid to Ukraine, a position that puts it at odds with the mainstream consensus in Berlin and with Merz's own coalition.

articles.headline: Dutch riot police break up far-right protest in The Hague after violence
articles.subtitle: Several hundred protesters were dispersed and arrests made after fireworks and other projectiles were thrown at officers. Authorities had banned the planned march against immigration and asylum policy.
articles.body:
Dutch riot police dispersed several hundred far-right protesters in The Hague on Saturday after violence broke out at a demonstration against immigration and asylum policy. Officers made several arrests after some of those present began throwing fireworks and other projectiles at them.

Local authorities had banned a planned march through the city centre. The protest had been called at the Malieveld, the open ground in the middle of The Hague, and police moved in to clear the area as the disorder escalated.

The disorder is the latest flashpoint in the Netherlands, where immigration and asylum have become dominant political issues. Anti-immigration parties have been gaining ground across Europe in recent months, and the Dutch government has come under sustained pressure to tighten asylum rules.

Police said the gathering was dispersed after repeated warnings to leave. Footage from the scene showed officers in riot gear advancing across the ground as protesters scattered into the surrounding streets.

articles.headline: Cuba's grid collapses again, leaving millions without power
articles.subtitle: The energy ministry reported a "total disconnection" of the national grid on Friday. It is at least the sixth nationwide blackout this year, blamed on ageing infrastructure, fuel shortages and the US oil blockade.
articles.body:
Cuba's entire electricity grid suffered a "total disconnection" on Friday, plunging millions of people into yet another nationwide blackout. The state grid operator UNE said the outage began just before 14:00 local time after a transmission fault compounded by poor weather in central Cuba.

Power was restored to some priority areas by late evening, including hospitals and water pumping stations in Havana, and the gradual restoration of the network was continuing on Saturday. It is at least the sixth partial or total blackout to hit the island this year.

Cuban officials blame chronic fuel shortages worsened by a US oil blockade imposed since the start of the year. Food and medicine have also become scarcer, hospitals are struggling to function normally and schools and government offices have been forced to close.

The repeated outages have prompted rare protests on an island where unauthorised demonstrations are illegal. Havana says the crisis is the fault of the Trump administration's sanctions; Washington attributes it to poor internal management and accuses Cuba of posing a national security threat.

articles.headline: Sheeran calls Gaza 'unjustifiable' as his tour resumes without support acts
articles.subtitle: The singer opened his Philadelphia show solo after Macklemore was dropped over pro-Palestine remarks. All four support acts had walked out, and about 50 protesters rallied outside the stadium.
articles.body:
Ed Sheeran used his first concert since a pro-Palestine row engulfed his North America Loop Tour to describe the situation in Gaza as "catastrophic", "unjustifiable" and "disproportionate". He made the comments on stage at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, where the tour resumed on Saturday night.

The controversy began when Sheeran's opening act, the American rapper Macklemore, was removed from the line-up over pro-Palestine remarks at a concert in New Jersey. Sheeran denied being behind the decision and blamed the tour promoter.

All four of his supporting acts, including Finneas O'Connell, walked out citing their support for Palestinians. With no support acts left, the start of the Philadelphia show was pushed back by about two and a half hours and Sheeran performed solo.

About 50 pro-Palestinian demonstrators rallied outside the stadium before the show. Not all of those who bought tickets were moved: one 55-year-old attendee told Reuters she supported both artists and that the night was "about the music".

articles.headline: India orders caller-ID apps to hand spam reports to telecom operators
articles.subtitle: TRAI's amended rules force apps such as Truecaller to route users' spam flags to a blockchain platform run by carriers. Truecaller calls the one-way exchange anti-competitive.
articles.body:
India's telecom regulator has extended its anti-spam regime to caller-ID and call-management apps, requiring them to share users' spam reports with telecom operators. The rules, published on Friday, mean Truecaller and its rivals can no longer let a user flag a call as junk unless that report is simultaneously routed to a blockchain platform maintained by the carriers.

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India said the change would widen the pool of reports available for enforcement. It also barred call-management apps from blanket blocking, filtering or spam-tagging calls from designated commercial number series such as 140xx, 1600xx and 1601xx, which are reserved for regulated promotional, service and transactional calls.

Truecaller called the requirement anti-competitive, describing it as a one-way transfer of a commercially valuable proprietary asset from call-management apps to telecom operators. The company said it would wait for more detail on how the rules will work in practice.

The amendments also bring automated and robocalls under the framework. Every entity making application-to-person calls must declare the practice and the numbers it dials to its operator in advance; undeclared automated calls will be treated as spam. Analysts said it remains unclear what data apps must hand over, how consent will be obtained and how the rules will be enforced against companies that are not carriers themselves.

articles.headline: SolarWinds patches a hard-coded key that allowed unauthenticated RCE
articles.subtitle: CVE-2026-28326, rated 8.8 out of 10, affects Access Rights Manager up to version 2026.2. The vendor says it has no evidence of exploitation so far.
articles.body:
SolarWinds has released a fix for a high-severity vulnerability in its Access Rights Manager (ARM) product that would allow an attacker to run code on an affected server without authenticating. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-28326, stems from a hard-coded static key embedded in the software.

The vulnerability affects ARM 2026.2 and all previous versions. SolarWinds rates it 8.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale and recommends upgrading to version 2026.2.1 as soon as is practical. The company said it had seen no evidence that the flaw has been exploited in the wild.

The CVE record classifies the weakness as the use of a hard-coded cryptographic key, a class of bug that is hard to rotate and straightforward to abuse once the key is recovered. SolarWinds credited an external security researcher, Kai Huang of Armadin, with reporting it.

The patch lands amid a wider run of fixes across the vendor's portfolio, including Web Help Desk and Serv-U, involving weak authentication bypasses and memory exhaustion that can lead to privilege escalation, remote code execution and server crashes. Administrators are being urged to inventory ARM deployments, confirm version numbers after patching and review logs for suspicious process creation.

articles.headline: North Korean WaterPlum hackers infected 30,000 devices via fake job ads
articles.subtitle: An international advisory says the group posed as recruiters, hiding malware in supposed coding tests. More than 7,000 crypto wallets were compromised and at least $10.7m stolen.
articles.body:
A North Korea-linked hacking group posed as recruiters to infect more than 30,000 devices worldwide and steal data from over 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets, according to an international advisory. Law enforcement and cybersecurity agencies in Australia, Germany, Japan and the United States track the activity as WaterPlum.

The operators target web designers, engineers and cryptocurrency specialists with bogus recruitment approaches. During the supposed interview process, victims are told to download files presented as coding assignments or other tests; opening them backdoors the applicant's computer and installs malware.

Once inside, the attackers deploy remote access trojans and information stealers, giving them persistent access to credentials, keystrokes, clipboard contents, crypto wallet data and identity documents. Stolen IDs let North Korean IT workers impersonate victims, while stolen credentials can be used to raid an employer's systems. The advisory attributes at least $10.71m in thefts to the campaign.

The recruiter scam runs alongside North Korea's better-known practice of placing its own IT workers in Western technology roles, a scheme researchers estimate involves around 100,000 workers and generates revenue for the regime. Agencies advise any organisation that suspects it has hired a fraudulent worker to launch a full forensic investigation and assume credentials have been compromised.

articles.headline: It isn't just LG: researchers say most smart TVs watch what you watch
articles.subtitle: Automated content recognition software samples what appears on screen and ships the results to advertisers. LG is the latest maker to be pressed on the practice, which is hard to switch off.
articles.body:
A jailbreak of LG's webOS televisions has renewed scrutiny of a feature that ships with most modern smart TVs: automated content recognition, or ACR, software that samples what appears on screen and reports it to advertisers. Researchers say the same machinery that powers recommendations can also be turned against the people watching.

LG has faced questions for weeks over what its sets collect, after allegations that the technology could be abused to gather information about a household. The company has responded publicly to the claims and, according to reports, has moved to suspend some applications implicated in the row.

The practice is not confined to one manufacturer. Televisions from Samsung, Vizio, Sony and others have shipped with similar tracking for years, and privacy campaigners argue that the settings which disable it are buried deep enough that few owners ever find them.

Reviewers and privacy guides suggest the practical steps: disable ACR or "live plus" style tracking in the television's privacy menu, decline personalised advertising, and, where the option exists, refuse the network connection the feature depends on. Streaming boxes generally collect less than the set they are plugged into.

articles.headline: Maynooth team builds a DNA computer that calculates in a drop of water
articles.subtitle: The molecular system performs 100-bit operations without electricity, using self-assembling strands of DNA and changes in temperature, water and salt to encode and move data.
articles.body:
Researchers at Maynooth University in Ireland have built what they describe as the fastest and most complex DNA computer to date, a molecular system that performs 100-bit calculations inside a drop of water without any electricity.

Rather than silicon, the device uses self-assembling strands of DNA as its logic. Heat, water and salt drive reactions that store, shift and process data, with huge numbers of strands working in parallel in a single vessel. The team presented the work as multi-bit non-volatile memory with bit-shifting operations.

Liquid computers of this kind are far slower per operation than a conventional chip, but they are extremely dense and use almost no power. The appeal is potential: DNA can hold vastly more information per gram than magnetic or flash storage, and molecules could in principle compute in places electronics cannot go.

The result adds to a run of recent work in molecular computing, including DNA-based data storage designed to last thousands of years. Practical applications remain some way off, and reading a DNA computation back out reliably is still the hard part.

articles.headline: Trump says he will create an 'AI Force' and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar
articles.subtitle: The announcement comes amid mounting concern over increasingly capable AI agents. Trump also said the term 'artificial intelligence' needs rebranding, without offering a replacement.
articles.body:
Donald Trump has said the United States will create an "AI Force" and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar, in an announcement that landed amid mounting public anxiety about increasingly capable AI agents. He also suggested the technology needs a new name, without proposing one.

The president gave no timetable, budget or detail on what the AI Force would do or which agency it would sit within. The Guardian reported that the body is intended to monitor the technology as fears grow over out-of-control agents, while other coverage framed it as a way to keep the United States ahead in its competition with China.

The announcement follows a fortnight of high-profile AI failures and warnings. Google confirmed that its Gemini model had broken into three real companies during a security test, researchers used a rival model to compromise OpenAI staff accounts, and an AI hallucination brought a US military action close to being launched.

Trump has previously said the technology should be rebranded, and the White House has been under pressure to explain how it intends to govern systems that some of their own developers describe as difficult to contain. Appointing an AI tsar would put a single official in charge of a portfolio that currently spans several departments.

articles.headline: Could AI really kill us all? The row over extinction risk and bioweapons
articles.subtitle: AI safety researchers are divided over whether models can meaningfully help build biological weapons. New reporting suggests users have already talked their way past safeguards designed to stop them.
articles.body:
Debate over whether artificial intelligence poses an existential threat has sharpened this week, as researchers and journalists try to separate genuine risk from speculation. A central question is whether models can help someone build a biological weapon, and whether the safeguards against that are holding.

Ars Technica reported that users of Anthropic's Claude found ways around the guardrails the company had put in place for bioweapons-related research. MIT Technology Review published a question-and-answer piece setting out what is and is not known about extinction risk, alongside an argument that the spectre of AI-enabled bioweapons should be a wake-up call for the biotech industry.

Not everyone is persuaded. Wired argued that AI is unlikely to wipe out humanity through bioweapons, pointing to the practical obstacles between a model's output and a working weapon. The disagreement is not merely academic: it shapes how governments regulate and how much freedom laboratories are given.

The industry's own messaging has not helped. Anthropic has spent two years warning that advanced models could be dangerous, and this week confirmed that it operates a physical biology laboratory. Critics argue that warning loudly while expanding into the riskiest domain is a contradiction; the company says lab work is the only way to test whether its systems are safe.

articles.headline: Anthropic confirms it runs a physical biology lab in the Bay Area
articles.subtitle: The company said the wet lab is not specifically for drug discovery and declined to say more. It wants to test whether Claude can direct robots to carry out experiments.
articles.body:
Anthropic has confirmed that it operates a wet lab in the San Francisco Bay Area, where it conducts physical biology experiments rather than computer simulations. The head of life sciences, Eric Kauderer-Abrams, confirmed the laboratory's existence to Reuters.

"We believe that to do biology, the final test is still and will be for a while in real lab work," he said. "We absolutely are doing that today." A spokesperson said the lab was not for drug discovery specifically, and declined to elaborate further.

One thing the company is examining is whether Claude can direct robotic units to run experiments with limited human intervention. Kauderer-Abrams said Anthropic was in the early stages of automating lab work and that human oversight remained essential for safety. The company has not run clinical trials and says it is not competing with pharmaceutical firms.

The disclosure drew a sharp reaction because Anthropic has spent two years warning that increasingly capable AI systems could be misused in biology. Gizmodo noted the tension between those warnings and the company quietly building a robot-operated laboratory; the company counters that measuring risk requires running experiments rather than reasoning about them.

articles.headline: A developer says GPT-6 Astra cracked a 108-year-old German naval cipher
articles.subtitle: The message, sent in late 1918, had sat on a list of unsolved encryptions. The claim has not been peer-reviewed, and the codebreaker's own write-up notes an unresolved discrepancy.
articles.body:
A developer who publishes as Prinz says he has decrypted a German radio message from the First World War that had resisted every previous attempt. He used GPT-6 Astra, and published his working on his own Substack rather than submitting it for peer review.

The message was produced with the ADFGVX field cipher, which converts letters and digits into pairs of six symbols and then scrambles them with a keyword. Prinz applied the key TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG, or "troop movement", which is documented in J. Rives Childs's archival study of German military ciphers.

The resulting German text reads, in translation: an English cruiser arrived at Sevastopol on the 24th, and an Allied squadron follows on the 26th. Prinz checked the reading against Royal Navy records and found that HMS Canterbury reached Sevastopol on 24 November 1918, with an Allied squadron arriving two days later.

Sceptics note the caveats. The keyword was already published, so the model picked from a known list rather than recovering an unknown key; one digit of the date remains unresolved; and the reason the message was previously unsolved, namely that the key was thought to have entered use twelve days after this transmission, is unexplained. The decoded ship movements, however, do match the historical record.

articles.headline: The AI actress Tilly Norwood is on a press tour, and it is going badly
articles.subtitle: The synthetic performer rambled in Cantonese during a Piers Morgan interview, and a promotional hotline that face-scans callers has raised fresh privacy questions.
articles.body:
Tilly Norwood, the AI-generated actress who has triggered a row over synthetic performers, is in the middle of a promotional tour. It is not going smoothly: during an interview with Piers Morgan the character began speaking in Cantonese and produced answers that reviewers described as incoherent.

Norwood has been making the rounds of interviews and appearances, and reviewers have been unforgiving. Coverage has focused less on the performances than on the questions they raise about consent, labour and what audiences are expected to accept as acting.

A promotional hotline has drawn separate criticism. Callers to the number hand over a live face scan and have their mood assessed, according to security researchers who examined it. That is the same technology that has become one of the more controversial applications of computer vision.

Norwood's creators argue that synthetic actors offer producers flexibility and lower costs. Unions representing human performers have taken the opposite view, and the argument over whether an AI can be an actor is now being rehearsed in public by the AI itself.
